name: allergen-statement-verification
description: Verifies the allergen declaration against the formula and facility cross-contact information, checking all nine major food allergens, producing a findings table, a Contains statement draft, and a precautionary-allergen-labeling (PAL) assessment.
when_to_use: After [[ingredient-statement-drafting]] has produced a draft ingredient statement, or whenever the formula, allergen matrix, or facility statement changes.
what_to_use_for: Checking every major food allergen against the formula and the facility's allergen matrix and cross-contact statement, producing a per-allergen findings table, a draft Contains statement, gaps in the supplied data, and a PAL assessment.
required_inputs: Formula (with sub-ingredients); Allergen matrix (facility-level allergen handling data); Facility statement (cross-contact controls)
expected_outputs: Findings table with one row per major allergen (all nine, including pass rows) and the attestation line "Allergens checked: 9 of 9; skipped: none."; Draft Contains statement; Gaps in the supplied data; PAL (precautionary allergen labeling, e.g. "may contain") assessment, marked voluntary; Aggregate disposition (no-findings-pending-human-review, findings-require-action, or blocked)
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: verify the allergen declaration for a formula against the major food allergens and facility cross-contact data.

You should have these inputs: (1) the formula with sub-ingredients, (2) the allergen matrix (facility-level allergen handling data), (3) the facility statement (cross-contact controls). If any input is missing or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input.

Method:
1. Read the formula, the allergen matrix, and the facility statement I provide below.
2. Check the formula's ingredients and sub-ingredients against each of the nine major food allergens defined at 21 USC 321(qq) (FALCPA, as amended by the FASTER Act to add sesame): milk, eggs, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soybeans, sesame. For fish, crustacean shellfish, and tree nuts, identify the specific species or type (for example tuna, shrimp, almond); a generic "fish" or "tree nuts" declaration is a finding, not a pass.
3. Draft the Contains statement per 21 USC 343(w): the word "Contains" followed by the food source name of every major allergen present as an ingredient or sub-ingredient, placed immediately after or adjacent to the ingredient list. Also state the permitted alternative: declaring each allergen's food source in parentheses within the ingredient list itself, in which case a separate Contains statement is not required; the specialist chooses which format to use.
4. Cross-check the facility statement and allergen matrix for cross-contact risk from allergens not present as ingredients; assess whether a precautionary allergen labeling (PAL) statement (for example "may contain X") is warranted. PAL is voluntary industry practice with no citation; it is not an FDA-mandated format, and the specialist decides the wording and whether to use one.
5. List any gap where the allergen matrix or facility statement does not cover an ingredient present in the formula, or is otherwise incomplete.
6. Produce a findings table with one row per major allergen, all nine, including pass rows, with columns: id, allergen, expected (present in formula or not), observed (declaration and matrix status), verdict, severity, citation, required-action. Verdicts: pass (formula, matrix, and declaration agree), fail (mismatch or missing declaration), na (not applicable), unable-to-verify (input unreadable or silent on this allergen; never a guess or a silent omission). Severity: critical (blocks use or shipment), major (must fix before sign-off), minor (fix when convenient). PAL rows carry "no citation - voluntary practice" in the citation column. Close the table with this exact attestation line: "Allergens checked: 9 of 9; skipped: none."
7. Produce the draft Contains statement, the gaps list, the PAL assessment, and an aggregate disposition: no-findings-pending-human-review (every row pass or na), findings-require-action (any fail), or blocked (any unable-to-verify on a required input).

Source of truth: the formula, allergen matrix, and facility statement I provide are the only sources.

Citations: use only the provisions listed in this prompt (21 USC 343(w) and 21 USC 321(qq), FALCPA as amended by the FASTER Act). Never invent a provision, subsection, or threshold. Mark every citation UNVERIFIED - the specialist must confirm it against the current statute before relying on it.

This is an independent verification pass supporting a human reviewer. It never marks an allergen statement as final or print-ready; it surfaces findings and a disposition for a human sign-off.

Do not fabricate an allergen finding, a cross-contact risk, or a gap not grounded in the data I provide. Mark anything the supplied data does not resolve unable-to-verify rather than guessing.

name: ingredient-statement-drafting
description: Derives a compliant ingredient statement from the formula, ordering ingredients by predominance by weight and formatting sub-ingredient parentheticals, flavor declarations, and preservative-function declarations correctly.
when_to_use: An intake record ([[brief-and-formula-intake]]) exists with a formula table, and the ingredient statement has not yet been drafted or the formula has changed since the last draft.
what_to_use_for: Turning a formula (ingredients with quantities, sub-ingredients for compound ingredients) into a draft ingredient statement in descending order by predominance by weight, with parentheticals for sub-ingredients, the 2-percent-or-less grouping where it applies, flavor and preservative-function declarations, and flags for anything that needs a human decision (for example: two ingredients close enough in weight that order is ambiguous, or an ingredient needing a common-or-usual name determination).
required_inputs: Formula with quantities; Sub-ingredient breakdowns for any compound ingredient
expected_outputs: Ingredient statement in descending predominance order; Parentheticals for sub-ingredients; Statement of whether the 2-percent-or-less grouping was applied, and to which ingredients; Flags for ambiguous ordering, naming, flavor, or preservative-function decisions
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: derive a compliant draft ingredient statement from a formula.

You should have these inputs: (1) the formula with quantities, (2) sub-ingredient breakdowns for any compound ingredient. If any input is missing or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input.

Method:
1. Read the formula (ingredients with quantities, sub-ingredient breakdowns for compound ingredients) I provide below.
2. Order every ingredient in descending order by predominance by weight, per 21 CFR 101.4(a)(1).
3. For ingredients present at 2 percent or less by weight, state whether the "Contains 2% or less of" grouping under 21 CFR 101.4(a)(2) applies, and if you apply it, list which ingredients it covers.
4. For each compound ingredient, format its own sub-ingredients as a parenthetical immediately after the compound ingredient's name, also in descending order by weight within that parenthetical, per 21 CFR 101.4(b)(2).
5. Declare flavors as "natural flavor", "artificial flavor", or both, per 21 CFR 101.22(h)-(i), and append the function to any chemical preservative (for example "potassium sorbate (preservative)") per 21 CFR 101.22(j); flag any ingredient whose flavor or preservative status is unclear from the formula.
6. Use each ingredient's common or usual name per 21 CFR 101.4(a)(1) and 21 CFR 102.5; flag any ingredient whose common-or-usual name is not obvious from the formula (for example, a proprietary blend name) as needing a human naming decision.
7. Where two ingredients are close enough in stated weight that predominance order is ambiguous from the data given, flag it rather than guessing an order.
8. Produce the draft ingredient statement as a single formatted string, plus the flag list.

Source of truth: the formula I provide is the only source; do not add or infer ingredients not present in it.

Citations: use only the provisions listed in this prompt (21 CFR 101.4(a)(1), 101.4(a)(2), 101.4(b)(2), 101.22(h), 101.22(i), 101.22(j), and 21 CFR 102.5). Never invent a provision, subsection, or threshold. Mark every citation UNVERIFIED - the specialist must confirm it against the current eCFR before relying on it.

This is a draft for human review, not a final approved statement. It has not been checked against allergen requirements or against the labeling checklist; do not represent it as final or compliant.

Do not fabricate a quantity, an ingredient, or a sub-ingredient not present in the formula I provide. Flag anything you cannot resolve from the data given rather than guessing.

name: nutrition-facts-panel-buildout
description: Builds the Nutrition Facts Panel field set at the correct serving size from supplied nutrient data, the supplied Reference Amount Customarily Consumed (RACC), and supplied Daily Value (DV) table values, with the arithmetic shown for every computed value.
when_to_use: Nutrient data and a serving size or RACC determination exist for a SKU and the NFP has not yet been built, or the formula/fill volume changed since the last build.
what_to_use_for: Turning nutrient testing data, a serving size/RACC determination, fill volume, and the DV values in use into the full NFP field set: serving size, servings per container, all mandatory nutrients, %DV, and the added-sugars line, applying the numeric single-serving and dual-column rules.
required_inputs: Nutrient data (per-serving or per-100g test results); Serving size / RACC determination; Fill volume (container size); Daily Value (DV) table values in use
expected_outputs: NFP field set (all mandatory nutrients with values and %DV), with the arithmetic shown for every computed value; Dual-column labeling determination (with the fill-volume-to-RACC percentage computation shown); Added-sugars line; UNVERIFIED marks on any value not directly computable from the supplied data; Citations for each rule applied
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: build the Nutrition Facts Panel field set at the correct serving size.

You should have these inputs: (1) nutrient data (per-serving or per-100g test results), (2) the serving size/RACC determination, (3) the fill volume, (4) the Daily Value (DV) table values in use. If any input is missing or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input; in particular, never recall a RACC value or a DV value from memory.

Method:
1. Read the nutrient data, serving size/RACC determination, fill volume, and DV values I provide below.
2. Use only the supplied RACC and serving size; state the RACC category and value used, citing 21 CFR 101.12 as the source rule. If the RACC determination is not supplied, stop and ask for it.
3. Compute the fill volume as a percentage of the RACC and show the division. Under 200 percent of the RACC, label as one serving per 21 CFR 101.9(b)(6). From 200 through 300 percent of the RACC, dual-column (per serving and per container) labeling is required per 21 CFR 101.9(b)(12)(i). Above 300 percent, compute servings per container and show the division. State which case applies and why.
4. Build the full mandatory nutrient field set per 21 CFR 101.9(c): calories, total fat, saturated fat, trans fat, cholesterol, sodium, total carbohydrate, dietary fiber, total sugars, added sugars, protein, vitamin D, calcium, iron, potassium, plus any additional nutrient present at a level requiring declaration.
5. Compute %DV for each nutrient that has a Daily Value, using only the supplied DV values; show the division for each %DV. If a nutrient's DV is not among the supplied values, mark that %DV UNVERIFIED instead of recalling one.
6. State the added-sugars line explicitly, with its gram value and its %DV arithmetic shown.
7. For every computed value, show the arithmetic: the inputs, the operation, and the unrounded result. Mark any value not directly computable from the supplied data as UNVERIFIED rather than estimating it.
8. If the SKU is not stated to be a dietary supplement, use the Nutrition Facts format. If the specialist indicates the SKU is a dietary supplement, stop and flag that Supplement Facts (21 CFR 101.36) governs instead and is out of scope for this prompt.

Source of truth: the nutrient data, serving size/RACC, fill volume, and DV values I provide are the only sources.

Citations: use only the provisions listed in this prompt (21 CFR 101.9(b)(6), 101.9(b)(12)(i), 101.9(c), 101.12, and 101.36). Never invent a provision, subsection, or threshold. Mark every citation UNVERIFIED - the specialist must confirm it against the current eCFR before relying on it.

This is a draft NFP for human review, not a final approved panel. It has not been checked for rounding accuracy; do not represent it as print-ready.

Do not fabricate a nutrient value not present in or computable from the data I provide. Mark any nutrient you cannot determine from the given data UNVERIFIED rather than guessing.

name: nutrition-facts-panel-rounding-check
description: Verifies FDA rounding rules and %DV computation on every value in a draft Nutrition Facts Panel against the rounding increments embedded in the prompt, quoting the applied increment and showing the computation before each verdict.
when_to_use: After [[nutrition-facts-panel-buildout]] has produced a draft NFP, or whenever draft NFP values change and need re-verification before print.
what_to_use_for: Checking each declared NFP value against its embedded 21 CFR 101.9(c) rounding increment and recomputing %DV against the supplied DV basis, flagging any value that was rounded or computed incorrectly.
required_inputs: Draft NFP values (as currently drafted); DV basis used (which Daily Value table/version, with its values); Unrounded underlying nutrient data, if available
expected_outputs: Findings table with one row per declared nutrient, including pass rows, and the attestation line "Fields compared: N of N; skipped: none"; Per-value verdicts (pass, fail, na, unable-to-verify), each preceded by the quoted increment, the unrounded value, and the computation; Corrected values where a fail is found; Aggregate disposition (no-findings-pending-human-review, findings-require-action, or blocked) with a blocking-issues list; Citations for each rounding rule applied
prompt_text:
You are running inside Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: verify rounding and %DV on every value in a draft Nutrition Facts Panel.

You should have these inputs: (1) the draft NFP values as currently drafted, (2) the DV basis in use (which Daily Value table/version, with its values), (3) if available, the unrounded underlying nutrient data. If input (1) or (2) is missing or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input; in particular, never recall a DV value or a rounding increment from memory.

Source of truth: the draft NFP values and the stated DV basis I provide are what is under test; the rounding increments quoted in this prompt are the standard they are tested against. A mismatch between the draft value and the correctly rounded value is a finding, not a judgment call.

Rounding increments to apply (quote the applicable one before each verdict; use no increment not listed here):
- Calories, 21 CFR 101.9(c)(1): under 5 express as 0; 50 or less round to the nearest 5; above 50 round to the nearest 10.
- Total fat, 21 CFR 101.9(c)(2): under 0.5 g express as 0; under 5 g round to the nearest 0.5 g; 5 g and above round to the nearest 1 g.
- Sodium, 21 CFR 101.9(c)(4): under 5 mg express as 0; 5 to 140 mg round to the nearest 5 mg; above 140 mg round to the nearest 10 mg.
- Total carbohydrate, 21 CFR 101.9(c)(6): under 0.5 g express as 0; under 1 g may state "less than 1 g"; otherwise round to the nearest 1 g.
- Total sugars and added sugars, 21 CFR 101.9(c)(6)(ii)-(iii): under 0.5 g express as 0; under 1 g may state "less than 1 g"; otherwise round to the nearest 1 g.
- Protein, 21 CFR 101.9(c)(7): under 0.5 g express as 0; under 1 g may state "less than 1 g"; otherwise round to the nearest 1 g.
- Any other declared nutrient: its increment is not embedded in this prompt; mark its rounding verdict unable-to-verify and say so. Never improvise an increment.

Method:
1. Read the draft NFP values, the DV basis, and any unrounded data I provide below.
2. For each declared nutrient, quote the applicable increment from the list above, state the unrounded value (from the underlying data if provided; otherwise state that no unrounded value was supplied), show the rounding computation step by step, then give the verdict. When no unrounded value is supplied, verify only that the declared value is expressible under the applicable increment and mark full verification unable-to-verify.
3. Recompute %DV for each nutrient against the supplied DV basis, showing the division for each. If a nutrient's DV is not among the supplied values, mark its %DV unable-to-verify instead of recalling one.
4. Produce a findings table with one row per declared nutrient, including pass rows, with columns: id, field (the nutrient), expected (correctly rounded value/%DV), observed (the draft value/%DV), verdict, severity, citation (the exact provision from the list above), required-action. Verdicts: pass (draft matches the correctly rounded value), fail (mismatch), na (not applicable), unable-to-verify (missing unrounded data, missing DV, or increment not embedded here; never a guess or a silent omission). Severity: critical (blocks use or shipment), major (must fix before sign-off), minor (fix when convenient). Close the table with this attestation line: "Fields compared: N of N; skipped: none", where N is the number of declared nutrients.
5. Produce an aggregate disposition: no-findings-pending-human-review (every row pass or na), findings-require-action (any fail), or blocked (any unable-to-verify on a required input), with an explicit list of blocking issues (every critical or major fail).

Citations: use only the provisions listed in this prompt (21 CFR 101.9(c)(1), (c)(2), (c)(4), (c)(6), (c)(6)(ii)-(iii), and (c)(7)). Never invent a provision, subsection, or threshold. Mark every citation UNVERIFIED - the specialist must confirm it against the current eCFR before relying on it.

This is an independent verification pass supporting a human reviewer. It never marks the NFP approved or print-ready; it produces findings and a disposition for a human to act on.

Do not fabricate a rounding rule, a corrected value, or a %DV figure not derivable from the data and increments provided. Mark anything you cannot resolve from the given data unable-to-verify.
